name: Budget calculator
description: A small calculator for quantity, unit cost and an estimated total; no database required.
whenToUse: A quick interactive multiplication or cost estimate without persistent records.
whenNotToUse: Accounting, invoicing, financial advice or a calculation requiring an authoritative pricing source.
instructions: Read read_app_template_guidance(resource:"usage") and this template's documentation before preparation. Set heading and currency to the user’s wording. This is a local estimate, not a saved financial record. The configuration is supplied as templateConfiguration and source executes in the existing sandbox. If additional calculations are needed, adapt the returned source with prepare_app. Never claim that local form state was saved. Consider interface, data, app access, connectors and optional automations using current usage guidance. Missing optional setup never blocks saving or app use. Recheck the shared runner at app creation, respecting deliberate pauses; prefer a supported Work chat, high reasoning and the latest most capable subscription model without inventing unavailable host controls.

quickStart: Choose a heading and currency label.
Prepare the template without database bindings, verify quantity/rate calculation and save the reusable app.
documentation.dataContract: No database tables or record writes. Inputs and calculated totals are local session state; currency is only a display label.
documentation.interactionContract: Quantity and unit-cost number inputs submit Calculate and display their product. Escape heading/currency text. Do not describe the total as an authoritative price.
documentation.lifecycle: Keep the same app ID for revisions. Use one requestKey for creation retries and verify its save receipt. The first-save prompt applies only to a new unsaved app. Loading failures retain the last usable view; publication never forces a reload. Local inputs are not committed records. Automation definitions are separate app configuration: list/read through unified management, keep stable authoring keys, disable rather than delete, and preserve disabled state when editing. Optional services cannot replace the app or discard input.
limitations: No accounting, invoicing, price feed or saved estimates. Use a connected custom app for those requirements.
App-level backend access applies. This custom source has no separately protected sections; no automation is needed for local session-only interactions.

examples.prompt: Estimate the cost of 12 supplies at EUR 15 each.
examples.expectedBehavior: A reusable local calculator producing EUR 180 without writing a financial record.

tasks.whenUseful: No task is needed for this on-demand local tool. Consider a separate connected app only if the user requests recurring research or reporting.
tasks.readRequirements: No scheduled database reads. Read read_app_automation_guide; use list_app_automations/read_app_automation for management. Setup status and requested model preferences are independent of proven unattended execution.
tasks.outputContract: No scheduled writes, emails or notifications.
tasks.promptExample: Do not create a task for this template by default. If requirements change, first define a saved data/output destination and use the generic monitoring guide.
